question: What primary factor guides the selection of essential drugs for a population?
explanation: Essential drugs focus specifically on addressing the most common and critical health problems faced by the majority of the population. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why must essential medicines remain affordable within a community?

options.A: To increase the import taxes on foreign companies
options.B: To guarantee high profits for local pharmacies
options.C: To discourage patients from visiting traditional healers
options.D: To prevent out-of-pocket financial ruin for patients

explanation: Affordability ensures that financial constraints do not prevent vulnerable individuals from accessing life-saving treatments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: In what year did the World Health Organization publish the first essential drug list?
explanation: The landmark WHO Expert Committee meeting in 1977 established the very first model list containing around 200 active substances. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: What main problem led to the creation of the essential drugs concept?

options.A: An excessive drop in pharmaceutical manufacturing companies
options.B: A sudden global shortage of basic chemical raw materials
options.C: Markets flooded with redundant and unproven brand-name drugs
options.D: The total collapse of international shipping lanes

explanation: Developing nations were wasting scarce resources on thousands of unnecessary and expensive brand-name medications before standardisation. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: How often does the WHO typically review and update its Model List of Essential Medicines?
explanation: Regular biennial reviews allow the WHO to incorporate new scientific breakthroughs and drop obsolete pharmaceutical agents. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which factor is NOT evaluated when deciding to add a drug to the essential list?

options.A: The public health relevance of the targeted disease
options.B: The scientific evidence supporting safety and efficacy
options.C: The overall cost-effectiveness of the treatment
options.D: The marketing budget of the manufacturing company

explanation: Selection committees rely strictly on clinical evidence, public health needs, and cost-effectiveness rather than commercial marketing budgets. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: How does an essential drug list improve safety for clinical staff?

options.A: By replacing traditional nursing documentation with automated software
options.B: By limiting the number of drugs workers must master, reducing prescribing errors
options.C: By completely eliminating the need for nurses to administer injections
options.D: By shifting all diagnostic responsibilities away from primary care clinics

explanation: Familiarity with a focused group of medicines helps clinicians know dosages, contraindications, and side effects thoroughly. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: What financial benefit does bulk-purchasing a limited set of medicines provide to health systems?

options.A: Higher taxes on imported medical devices
options.B: Lower prices through economies of scale
options.D: Increased inflation in local drug markets

explanation: Purchasing large quantities of standardized medications drives down unit costs for healthcare institutions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why might a rigid essential drug list fail to meet all community needs during a health transition?

options.A: It may lag behind emerging chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: It automatically increases the cost of surgical equipment
options.C: It forces manufacturing companies to shut down local factories
options.D: It prevents nurses from administering basic first aid

explanation: When disease burdens shift rapidly from infectious illnesses to chronic conditions, static formularies can be slow to adapt. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: What common supply chain issue compromises heat-sensitive medicines in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Poor storage infrastructure and temperature control
options.B: Overproduction of tablets by local factories
options.C: Frequent changes in international currency rates
options.D: Excessive use of digital inventory scanners

explanation: Inadequate cold chain equipment and poor warehouse conditions degrade the potency of temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary document derived from the National Drug Policy for public health facilities in Nigeria?
explanation: The Essential Medicines List dictates the approved inventory of pharmaceuticals for public healthcare institutions in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: How does local pharmaceutical manufacturing support the goals of Nigeria's National Drug Policy?

options.A: By reducing national dependence on costly pharmaceutical importation
options.B: By stopping all clinical research conducted by foreign universities
options.C: By eliminating the need for regulatory enforcement agencies
options.D: By guaranteeing free medication for every citizen in private hospitals

explanation: Encouraging domestic production of essential drugs ensures sustainable supply chains and lowers foreign exchange burdens. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)
